title: Delta-eval harness for quant variants and adaptive pin suggester
creator: Samantha Lee
description: Build an automated delta-eval harness that runs pairwise comparisons between a floating-point baseline and newly produced low-precision variants (INT8/GPTQ/AWQ/FP8). The harness will produce a compact difference profile (delta metrics) used to: 1) flag candidate regressions, 2) generate an adaptive pin suggestion score for model-variant pinning in the pin registry, and 3) feed the nightly regression detector and canary rollout decisions. This ticket covers the evaluation orchestration, scoring heuristics, and initial integration into the pin suggestion API and release pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can execute a reproducible pairwise run across 10k representative prompts within a sandboxed environment and output a delta summary (latency, token-LL, ROUGE/EM proxies, embedding-distance, and top-k token shifts).
Adaptive pin score generated for each variant and stored in the pin registry with rationale fields (latency_gain_pct, quality_delta_score, drift_flag).
Automated blocker: variants with quality_delta_score > 0.12 or embedding-distance > 0.25 must fail canary by default; canary run shows correct fail/pass decisions on synthetic regressions.
Telemetry produced is ingested by the nightly regression job and visible in Console per-variant dashboard within runtime-1.21 release window.
design_notes: We will evaluate deltas across multiple axes: token-level log-likelihood delta (LLD), macro-quality proxies (ROUGE-L on synthetic evals, exact-match on selected tasks), embedding-based centroid distance on multiple prompt categories, and latency P50/P95. Scoring heuristic: quality_delta_score = weighted_sum(normalized_LLD, 1 - normalized_embedding_sim, macro_quality_drop). Default weights 0.5/0.3/0.2. Pin score combines latency savings and quality_delta_score into a single 0-1 suggested_pin_confidence. The harness should be model-agnostic and accept a "variant descriptor" pointing to artifact + quant-profile metadata. Use dockerized executor with cached KV to replicate runtime tokenization and KV cache behavior.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Orchestrator and runner - implement a lightweight job runner that pulls baseline and variant artifacts, runs pairwise prompts, and emits raw per-prompt traces (start-end timestamps, per-token LL, tokens generated).
Phase 2: Scoring service - compute delta metrics and produce the adaptive pin score; store outputs in pin registry schema extension (fields: pin_confidence, reasons, metric_breakdown).
Phase 3: Integration - wire pin suggestions into the existing pin approval UI and the canary pipeline; add endpoints for 'recommend_pin' with dry-run and explainability payloads.
Phase 4: Telemetry & dashboards - emit metrics to the Console (per-variant panel) and add alert rules for nightly regression detection.
test_plan: Unit tests for scoring heuristics with synthetic distributions (sensitivity of weights).
Integration test: run harness in CI with small prompt pack (100 prompts) verifying reproducibility and numerical stability.
Smoke canary: deploy two engineered regressions (perturbed quant matrix and intentional weight corruption) to validate fail paths and rollback automation.
Load test: run harness across 10k prompts and ensure job completes within acceptable wall time on a single p3.2xlarge-equivalent instance (target < 6h).
rollout_plan: Start with internal-only run for newly onboarded variants. Nightly job will populate candidate pin suggestions tagged 'internal-suggest'. After 2 full cycles without false positives, enable 'auto-suggest' flag for PM review. For high-confidence pins (pin_confidence >= 0.9 and quality_delta_score < 0.02) we will auto-propose to the pin registry; for medium-confidence (0.6-0.9) create a PM approval task. Rollback: if canary observes metric regressions post-rollout we automatically create a roll-forward ticket and mark the pin as 'quarantined' and surface the reason and the per-prompt counterexamples in Console.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-reliance on synthetic proxies can miss UI-level regressions. Mitigation: include a small human-curation set for critical tasks and sample live requests (sanitized) where allowed.

Risk: Pin suggester misclassifies noisy variants as safe and causes customer impact. Mitigation: conservative default thresholds, require PM approval for medium-confidence pins, and initial 'internal-only' mode.

Risk: Compute cost of full delta runs for every variant. Mitigation: two-stage evaluation (cheap smoke on 500 prompts -> if pass, expanded 10k run); reuse cached tokenization and KV where possible to reduce runtime.
